sn35.1:1.1: The “interior” aspects of the sense fields are the sensory organs starting with the “eye”, as opposed to the sense stimuli starting with “sights”, which are “exterior” (_bāhira_). | _Ajjhatika/bāhiya_ (“interior/exterior”) are used for the senses because they typically refer to inner and outer aspects of a thing, in this case, of the individual. The similar pair _ajjhatta/bahiddha_ (“internal/external” or “inside/outside”) typically indicates the relation of two things to each other (see [sn35.69:1.4]()). Thus a house may have its interior painted white and exterior painted blue, while a woman might be inside the house or outside of it.  This distinction seems in line with Vedic usage. For _bahirdhā_, Chāndogya Upaniṣad 3.12.7 mentions “what is outside a person”;  it’s also someone who is “outside” the sacrifice (eg. Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.9.2.2). _Bāhya_ is used more in philosophical contexts, where it sometimes contrasts with _ādhyātmika_ (Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad Kārikā 2.38) but more commonly _antara_: “As a man embraced by a woman he loves is oblivious to everything within or without, so this person embraced by the self consisting of knowledge is oblivious to everything within or without“ (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 4.3.21, Olivelle translation). See also note on [sn35.4:1.5]().
